classification.difficultyReason: Find interior angles from exterior angles, then use the triangle angle sum to identify equal angles.

content.prompt: Decide whether the triangles shown are isosceles.

spec.description: Unfilled triangle with a vertical right side and the left side extended beyond its upper vertex. The upper-left exterior angle is 139 degrees and the upper-right interior angle is 98 degrees. No equal-side marks or angle arcs are supplied.
spec.mathematics: The interior angle supplementary to 139 degrees is 41 degrees. The remaining interior angle is also 41 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 139-degree and 98-degree labels are visible in the question.

answer.worked:
The upper-left interior angle is supplementary to $139^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Upper-left angle} &= 180^{\circ}-139^{\circ}\\ &=41^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bottom angle}+41^{\circ}+98^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\\text{Bottom angle}+139^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\\text{Bottom angle}&=41^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Yes. Two angles are $41^{\circ}$, so their opposite sides are equal and the triangle is isosceles.

spec.description: Three extended straight lines enclose a triangle. Preserve both extensions of each line. The left vertex has exterior angle 112 degrees, and the upper vertex has exterior angle 124 degrees. No equal-side marks or angle arcs are supplied.
spec.mathematics: The left and upper interior angles are 68 degrees and 56 degrees. The remaining interior angle is 56 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 112-degree and 124-degree labels are visible in the question.

answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Left interior angle}&=180^{\circ}-112^{\circ}\\&=68^{\circ},\\\text{Upper interior angle}&=180^{\circ}-124^{\circ}\\&=56^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Remaining angle}+68^{\circ}+56^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\\text{Remaining angle}+124^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\\text{Remaining angle}&=56^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Yes. Two angles are $56^{\circ}$, so their opposite sides are equal and the triangle is isosceles.
